evidence.note: claim: refusal paths print stderr only; observed on main in a temp repo: 'ddflow --json search x --source bogus' rc=3 stdout empty; sweep over 140 leaf commands failed on ~38 (refusal/error/nothing with empty stdout) before the fix

commit: central body-on-every-exit in cli.main plus viewers_search refusal body

chunk_findings.detail:
In the `REFUSED` branch the new body is built with `emit_json({"rows": [], "total": 0, **out.data, "reason": out.reason})`, i.e. it unpacks `out.data`. On a refusal the `view_read` answer carries only a reason — that is exactly why the previous code never dereferenced `out.data` on this path, and why the CLI's own catch-all synthesizes the refusal body from `refusal_body(code, said.text)` with no `rows`/`total` at all. If `out.data` is `None` (the natural value for a reason-only answer, and the value the old code tolerated by never touching it), `{**None}` raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not a mapping`; the same happens if `out.data` is a bare row list (`'list' object is not a mapping`).

Demonstration: `ddflow --json session list --state bogus` (and `ddflow --json search foo --source bogus`). `view_head` raises before `emit_json` runs, so the new CLI wrapper's `except BaseException` / `exit_for(exc)` catches it: nothing was emitted yet (`bodies_emitted() == before`), so the wrapper prints `TypeError: ...` to stderr and emits `refusal_body(1, "TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not a mapping")` to stdout. stdout is therefore non-empty JSON, but the result is now an *error* body with rc 1 instead of the intended refusal body carrying `rows: []` with rc 3 — the very regression the change set out to fix (refusal reason lost, exit code changed). The stated regression check "parses the stdout of both" cannot catch this, because stdout is still parseable JSON; only the exit code and `reason` content are wrong.

chunk_findings.detail: `_Tee` subclasses `io.TextIOBase` and overrides only `write`/`flush`, so it does not forward any attribute access to the wrapped stream it is standing in for. `io.TextIOBase` inherits the base implementations from `io.IOBase`, which means that while `remembered_stderr()` is active, the process-wide `sys.stderr` is no longer a faithful stderr: `sys.stderr.isatty()` returns `False` unconditionally (even when the real stderr is a terminal), `sys.stderr.writable()` returns `False`, `sys.stderr.fileno()` raises (`OSError`/`io.UnsupportedOperation`) instead of returning the real descriptor, and `encoding`/`errors`/`buffer` are absent or `None`. Because `remembered_stderr` swaps `sys.stderr` for the whole region it wraps (that is the point of the context manager), every library call made inside that region sees the degraded object. Concrete failures: a colorizer that gates on `file.isatty()` (click/`secho(err=True)`, rich, or ddflow's own helper) silently drops its ANSI styling on an interactive terminal; anything doing `os.isatty(sys.stderr.fileno())` or `subprocess.run(..., stderr=sys.stderr)` raises `OSError: fileno` where it previously worked; and a writer that guards on `if stream.writable():` produces no output at all, which also means nothing reaches `_Tee.text`, so `refusal_body` falls back to `{"refusal": "exit 3"}` and loses the very reason the fix was added to surface. A proxy whose stated contract is "stderr that also remembers what was written to it" should delegate `isatty`/`writable`/`fileno`/`encoding`/`errors`/`buffer` to `self.inner` (or at least set `isatty`/`writable` from the inner stream) rather than inheriting `IOBase`'s non-interactive defaults.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/render.py:_Tee (installed by `remembered_stderr`)

chunk_findings.detail: The sweep runs every leaf command as 8 concurrent subprocesses (`ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8)` mapped over `LEAVES`, each `_run` invoking `sys.executable -m ddflow ...` against the single `repo` prepared once by `run_cli(repo, "init")`). Several of those leaves mutate shared on-disk state rather than refusing early: `init` itself has no required arguments, so `_argv` returns just `["init"]` and it actually re-executes concurrently with the readers; and for any required argument that carries `choices`, `_argv` substitutes the *first valid choice* (`a.choices and next(iter(a.choices)) or BOGUS`, line ~53) instead of a bogus value, so those commands take their real action instead of stopping at a refusal. Two concurrent writers on the repo's state (sqlite/file) then yield `database is locked` / partial-read errors whose stderr is a text traceback and whose stdout is empty; `json.loads(p.stdout)` raises, `p.returncode != 0`, and the command is appended to `bad`, e.g. `task list: rc=1 stdout=''`, failing the assertion on code that is actually correct. The result is timing/order dependent: the same test passes or fails run-to-run depending on which subprocesses overlap, and it also can fail deterministically if any of the non-allowlisted leaves (e.g. `init` on an already-initialized repo) refuses with a text body, since the allowlists `LONG_RUNNING`/`TEXT_ONLY` do not cover it.
